newDescription:
In this Year 6 English lesson, pupils learn how cohesion helps ideas link smoothly within and across paragraphs, and how to use a range of cohesive devices to make writing clearer and easier to follow.

This lesson includes:
✔ Revisiting what paragraphs are and when to start a new paragraph
✔ Understanding cohesion as the way ideas link together within and across paragraphs
✔ Using repetition of key words and related words to maintain a clear topic
✔ Using pronouns and other references to avoid unnecessary repetition
✔ Using cohesive adverbials for time, contrast, emphasis, cause and effect, place, number, exception, comparison and clarification
✔ Checking paragraph order and relevance so related ideas stay together
✔ Using ellipsis to omit words that the reader can already infer
✔ Understanding that ellipsis can improve clarity and reduce repetition even when no three dots are used
✔ Applying cohesive devices across more than one paragraph
✔ Writing and reviewing a multi-paragraph text with repetition, adverbials, order, relevance and ellipsis
✔ Planning and writing a fact sheet in which each paragraph has a clear focus and ideas are linked across the whole text

Pupils begin by revisiting the purpose of paragraphs and exploring how cohesion acts like glue, holding ideas together so a text flows from beginning to end.

The lesson then examines several cohesive devices in detail. Pupils analyse repetition, explore different groups of cohesive adverbials, and learn how order and relevance help maintain a logical flow. They also study ellipsis as a way of leaving out information that can already be understood.

Pupils apply these ideas in a short multi-paragraph writing task before using a fictional animal fact sheet to practise organising information, grouping related details and choosing suitable cohesive devices across paragraphs.

By the end of the lesson, learners will be able to create cohesion across paragraphs using adverbials, repetition, ellipsis, careful ordering and relevant detail.
